entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Praejectus, Prejectus or Projectus (625–676) was a bishop of Clermont, who was killed together with the abbot Amarinus as a result of contemporary political struggles.


Praejectus was a key figure in the tumultuous 7th century, when the Frankish kingdom was undergoing significant transformations. His position as bishop of Clermont placed him at the intersection of ecclesiastical and secular power struggles.


The murder of Praejectus and Amarinus in 676 serves as a stark reminder of the violent politics of the time, as various factions vied for control of the Frankish kingdom. This event would have far-reaching consequences for the development of Christianity in Western Europe.


The legacy of Praejectus can be seen in the subsequent struggles for power and influence in the Frankish kingdom, particularly during the reign of King Dagobert I. His death marked the beginning of a period of instability that would eventually lead to the Carolingian Renaissance.


The final sentence of this summary reads: The Carolingian Renaissance, which would see the rise of Charlemagne, was in part a response to the power vacuum left by Praejectus's murder, as various factions sought to consolidate their influence in the face of an increasingly complex web of alliances and rivalries.
